newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca says incident at UK plant under control.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca says incident at UK plant under control.

text.p: British pharmaceutical company Zeneca Group Plc said an incident at its Grangemouth chemical plant on Thursday, which led to an emergency being declared, was now under control.

A "fume release" at 0640 GMT at its pigment manufacturing plant in central Scotland was of a volume to have had the "potential for impact beyond the works boundary (that) an emergency was declared," Zeneca said in a statement.
It said emergency services had helped in dealing with the incident, in which one individual was sent to hospital as a precautionary measure.
A clean-up and full enquiry were underway, Zeneca said.
The Press Association (PA) reported that the plant was sealed off for around 90 minutes after aluminium chloride leaked into the drainage system, resulting in the formation of hydrochloric acid.
The PA quoted a police spokesman as saying: "There was no danger to the public. Everything was done as a precaution".
